Sales & Property Tax Refund for Senior & Disabled Citizens:
This program offers eligible senior citizens and disabled individuals to receive a yearly refund of sales or property taxes. Returns are calculated based on your income; the Special Tax Division begins issuing refund checks at the beginning of September.
Eligibility Requirements:
The applicant was a South Dakota resident during the entire prior calendar year.
The applicant reached the age of 65 on or before January 1 of the current year OR disabled ( as defined by the Social Security Act ).
Applicants who live alone and have a yearly income under $14,949 or live in a household whose members’ combined income is under $20,141?
For an application click here and mail your request to the Department of Revenue, Special Tax Division, 445 East Capitol Avenue, Pierre, SD 57501-3185 or submit online at https://sddor.seamlessdocs.com/f/2050 Applications are accepted from May 1 to July 1.
Assessment Freeze for the Elderly & Disabled
What the Program Does
This program reduces the assessed value of the homeowner’s property. Property is defined as the house, a garage, and the lot upon which it sits or one acre, whichever is less. Additional information is available in our Freeze on Assessments: Dwellings of Disabled and Senior Citizens Brochure (PDF) .
To Be Eligible
Must be 65 years of age or older OR disabled ( as defined by the Social Security Act ).
Must own the home or retain a life estate in the property.
Un-remarried widow/widowers of persons previously qualified may still qualify in some circumstances.
Have resided for at least 200 days of the previous calendar year in the single-family dwelling.
Income and property value limits apply.
To Apply
Applications are available online or at any county treasurer’s office beginning in January of each year and must be submitted annually to the local county treasurer’s office on or before April 1st.

Announcements
All Commission Meetings will be at the Commission Meeting Room next to the Law Enforcement Center. Check upcoming events for those dates.
The Treasurer’s Office public serving hours are from 8:30 am – 4:30 pm Monday thru Friday. This will include phone calls and in person. This will allow the treasurer’s office time in the morning to balance the previous day and prepare the required documents to be sent to Pierre without interruption.
For the Sheriff’s Office/911 after hour requests will need to be handled by calling our office (605-448-5181) so we can assist you. With the new addition our S.O./911 will finally be in full compliance with security rules we are required to follow. The best option for any requests/needs is to call before stopping in.
